title.en: The Past Simple: irregular verbs (went, saw, bought)
title.es: El Pasado Simple: verbos irregulares (went, saw, bought)

text.en: The past of irregular verbs does not end in -ed; it is a separate form you have to learn: go → went, buy → bought, see → saw. Spanish has irregular forms too (fui, hice, tuve), so the idea is familiar. The irregular form appears only in affirmative sentences; in negatives and questions you need “didn’t” and “did” exactly as with regular verbs, and the verb goes back to its base form.
text.es: El pasado de los verbos irregulares no termina en -ed; es una forma aparte que hay que aprender: go → went, buy → bought, see → saw. El español también tiene formas irregulares (fui, hice, tuve), así que la idea es conocida. La forma irregular solo aparece en las oraciones afirmativas; en negaciones y preguntas hacen falta «didn’t» y «did» igual que con los verbos regulares, y el verbo vuelve a su forma base.

text.en: Statement: the irregular form, the same for every person: I went, she went, they went.
text.es: Afirmación: la forma irregular, igual para todas las personas: I went, she went, they went.

examples.es: I went to the market yesterday.

tr.en: I went to the market yesterday.

text.en: Negatives and questions: didn’t / did + BASE VERB. The verb does not stay in the past form: I didn’t go, Did you go? (not “didn’t went”).
text.es: Negación y pregunta: didn’t / did + VERBO BASE. El verbo no se queda en pasado: I didn’t go, Did you go? (no «didn’t went»).

title.en: The past of to be: was / were
title.es: El pasado de to be: was / were

text.en: I / he / she / it: WAS. You / we / they: WERE. Negative: wasn’t, weren’t. Question: Was / Were + subject. There is no “did” with to be.
text.es: I / he / she / it: WAS. You / we / they: WERE. Negación: wasn’t, weren’t. Pregunta: Was / Were + sujeto. Con to be no hay «did».

examples.es: Were you at home last night?

tr.en: Were you at home last night?

text.en: Do not add -ed to irregular verbs. Do not say “I goed” or “She buyed”; say “I went”, “She bought”.
text.es: No añadas -ed a los verbos irregulares. No digas «I goed» ni «She buyed», di «I went», «She bought».

text.en: In questions and negatives the verb stays in its base form. Do not say “Did you went?” or “I didn’t saw”; say “Did you go?” and “I didn’t see”.
text.es: En preguntas y negaciones el verbo se queda en forma base. No digas «Did you went?» ni «I didn’t saw», di «Did you go?» y «I didn’t see».

text.en: With the past of to be there is no “did”, and each person has its own form. Do not say “I were” or “We was”; say “I was”, “We were”.
text.es: Con el pasado de to be no hay «did», y cada persona tiene su forma. No digas «I were» ni «We was», di «I was», «We were».

text.en: Learn the irregular forms by repetition. The most frequent ones: was/were, had, went, did, saw, made, took, came, got, said.
text.es: Aprende las formas irregulares repitiéndolas. Las más frecuentes: was/were, had, went, did, saw, made, took, came, got, said.

speak.en: The past of irregular verbs is a separate form you have to learn: «go», «went», «buy», «bought», «see», «saw», «eat», «ate», «take», «took». It is the same for every person: «I went», «she went», «they went». In negatives and questions the verb goes back to its base form: «I didn't go», «Did you go?». The past of to be is «was» or «were»: «I was», «you were», «he was», «we were». Careful: not «I goed», not «did you went» and not «I were».
speak.es: El pasado de los verbos irregulares es una forma aparte que hay que aprender: «go», «went», «buy», «bought», «see», «saw», «eat», «ate», «take», «took». Es igual para todas las personas: «I went», «she went», «they went». En negaciones y preguntas el verbo vuelve a su forma base: «I didn't go», «Did you go?». El pasado de to be es «was» o «were»: «I was», «you were», «he was», «we were». Cuidado: no «I goed», no «did you went» y no «I were».

why.en: The past of go is irregular: went. “Yesterday” shows the past: I went to the market.
why.es: El pasado de go es irregular: went. «Yesterday» indica pasado: I went to the market.

goed.en: “Goed” does not exist; go is irregular: went.
goed.es: «Goed» no existe; go es irregular: went.

go.es: «Go» es presente; «yesterday» es pasado, por eso «went».

wrong.en: In a statement there is no “did”: the irregular verb itself carries the past (went).
wrong.es: En una afirmación no hay «did»: el propio verbo irregular lleva el pasado (went).

went.en: The past is already in “didn’t”; the base verb follows: go, not “went”.

wrong.en: The past is already in “did”; putting the verb in the past too would mark it twice: “Did you went?” is wrong.
wrong.es: El pasado ya está en «did»; poner también el verbo en pasado lo marcaría dos veces: «Did you went?» es incorrecto.

text.en: go is present here, because the question is about now
text.es: go es aquí presente, porque la pregunta es sobre ahora

wrong.en: “Did” shows the past; “go” is just the base form, not the present tense.

why.en: A past question starts with Did, followed by the base verb: Did you go to the party?
why.es: Una pregunta en pasado empieza con Did, seguido del verbo base: Did you go to the party?

Were.en: “Were” is the past of to be; “go” is a normal verb, so “Did you go?”.
Were.es: «Were» es el pasado de to be; «go» es un verbo normal, por eso «Did you go?».

tr.en: Did you go to the party?
